title: Growing up poor but sheltered in an all-black Oklahoma town
summary: As the baby of a musical family he never knew hard times, though his widowed mother farmed; his sisters played piano and brothers sang; he walked miles to hear country picnic music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was from a musical family. As a kid--by being the baby--the nearest one to me was twelve years older than me, so you understand, I was really the baby. And seemingly, although a poor family, they, by losing my father, they were determined that I wouldn't want for anything, and all along they're just human; but I don't think they spoiled me by doing it, but as I said, I didn't know anything at all
about hard times, although we had nothing. And I never was known to be hungry, although we had nothing.
As I got older I wondered a lot of times how in the world my mother even managed to get along with what little we did, trying to farm around.

They wouldn't take me out of school to do any kind of work; whatever I did it had to be after school. As I said, the family, the two girls both played piano and the boys had a little singing quartet and they would sing around. I got a very big kick out of it, but never, never dreamed that I would be--that that would be my livelihood, and at that time, as a kid, they would have the little country picnics and they would have somebody playing, maybe one horn or guitar or piano up on a wooden platform, and I would walk miles to hear that which I enjoyed but looked like no bug was on me to really learn how to play anything.
No, that was in Tulsa; that was in Taft, Oklahoma. I might have missed a point. My family moved to Oklahoma when I was maybe a little less than a year old, and I never did even know my father.
You moved there in your infancy?
